claims.text: Increasing Cr content promotes formation of protective Cr2O3 scales in multiprincipal-element alloys.
Increasing Al content promotes formation of protective Al2O3 scales in multiprincipal-element alloys.
Dense, continuous, adherent protective oxide scales suppress inward oxygen diffusion and outward metal transport, thereby slowing oxidation.
Cr and Al act synergistically in forming chromia- or alumina-based surface layers.
The Cr/Al-driven oxide-scale mechanism governs oxidation resistance across multiprincipal-element alloys.
Protective chromia or alumina scales preserve mechanical integrity and prevent microstructural degradation during long-term high-temperature exposure.
The proposed baseline alloy contains approximately 5 at.% Cr and approximately 5 at.% Al.
Cr and/or Al will be increased to approximately 15–20 at.% to promote protective oxide formation.
The relevant structural mediator is a continuous, slow-growing Cr2O3 or alpha-Al2O3 surface scale.
Such scales reduce oxygen ingress and depletion of metallic elements from the underlying alloy.
Elevated Cr and Al levels favor the early development and maintenance of dense, adherent oxide layers.
Dense, adherent oxide layers impede both inward oxygen diffusion and outward metallic diffusion.
Increasing protective-element levels will produce approximately 30–50% lower oxidation mass gain than the baseline.
Increasing protective-element levels will reduce microstructural deterioration relative to the baseline.
A baseline containing about 5 at.% Cr and Al will form less protective, more rapidly growing oxide scales than the enriched variants.
The hypothesis is valid primarily for total Cr+Al contents up to approximately 20 at.%, temperatures of 900–1200 °C, and exposures of approximately 100 hours.
Other oxide-forming elements such as Mn can alter scale composition, integrity, and adhesion.
Longer-term tests are required to establish conclusive Cr/Al synergy thresholds.
Failure of Cr/Al enrichment to reduce oxidation rates or produce stable protective scales relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: Cr/Al enrichment is variously described as reaching 15–20 at.% without consistently specifying whether this applies to each element or their sum; the boundary instead specifies total Cr+Al up to about 20 at.%.

The design says Cr/Al atomic percentages will increase while all other element concentrations remain fixed. Because atomic percentages must normalize to 100%, both cannot be true unless the balancing element or renormalization procedure is specified.
